- Z427 (2026-10-04, D37's /spec): Cmd+Z after Format Document on a `.tex` file does not undo the format (D14's look, with `latex.formatter: tex-fmt`), though typing is undone. Its cause was not found by reading: Monaco 0.57 pushes undo stops around a format's edit, the page's formatter is Monaco's own provider, the page frees only Cmd+K and Ctrl+K from Monaco, and the editor's model is made again only on a new name or path. No probe could be run without a formatter set, since the page's Monaco is not reachable from a script and `latex.formatter` is `none`. D37 is built without this defect; the other twelve go ahead. Options: (a) a diagnosis on TEST now, in parallel with D37's build: set `latex.formatter` to `tex-fmt` in `config/behavior.yml` for the probe (one write, recorded in History, put back afterwards and its hash checked, as D14's look did), format a scratch `.tex` file in `zz-look-d37/` at the hub root, and probe Cmd+Z; the found fix joins D37 as its first repair round when it is found before D37 lands, else a small step after it; pro: the cause is found while D37 is still open; con: a config write and a scratch folder on the hub for the length of the probe. (b) D37 lands first and the diagnosis runs at its landing look, which opens TEST anyway; pro: one look instead of two; con: the fix then needs its own step. (c) drop the defect; con: HELP.md keeps saying undo takes the format back, which is false. Recommendation: (a), since it finds the cause before D37 lands and keeps the fix inside D37. (c) is the lazy one. Closed 2026-10-05 in automode: (a).

- Z305 (2026-10-03 01:00, Axel): (a), each placeholder's value reaches the shell as an environment variable (`"$OCULUS_ARG_<n>"`) and the tokenizer and its refusals go; built at D17's landing on main, with tests that run every route of D17's round 2 review through real `/bin/sh` and create nothing. The item as raised: Z305 (2026-10-03, D17's round 2 review): a selection can still run as a command. D17's placeholders (`${selectedText}`, `${file}` and the others) are filled into a command line as one single-quoted word, and a check refuses a placeholder inside quotes, after a backslash or in a comment. The review of round 2 (`agents/reviews/D17-refuter.md`, "Repair round 2, refuted", ruling 1) got a selection holding `$(touch m)` or `; touch m` to run through real `/bin/sh` by eight routes the check passes: a here-doc body (`cat <<EOF`), an apostrophe in a here-doc body, double quotes nested in `$(...)`, a `#` after an escaped blank or a backslash-newline, a placeholder right after `$` (`$${selectedText}`, which turns the quoting into `$'...'`), and arithmetic `$((${selectedText}))`. Each needs a run line written that way in a repository's `.oculus/commands.yml` and approved by you; the selection is what runs unapproved. D17's two repair rounds are spent, so this is a fix at landing or a ruling. What VS Code does: tasks.json substitutes `${selectedText}` into the command line as raw text with no quoting and no check, so a selection runs as shell text whenever the line puts it there. Options: (a) values reach the shell as environment variables: each placeholder is replaced by `"$OCULUS_ARG_<n>"` and the value is set in the task's environment, so the shell never parses the value as code, in any context; the tokenizer and its refusals go. What stays open is a line that re-evaluates text itself (`eval`, `bash -c "$OCULUS_ARG_1"`, `$((...))` arithmetic), which the approved text shows plainly. For: ends the cause rather than chasing contexts; less code than the tokenizer. Against: a placeholder inside a quoted string now reads as the variable's text (`echo "file: ${file}"` still works, since `"$OCULUS_ARG_1"` inside double quotes expands; inside single quotes it prints the variable name), and the line the terminal shows names the variable, not the value. Done by me at D17's landing, with tests that run every route above through real `/bin/sh` and create nothing. (b) Extend the tokenizer with a mode stack for `$(`, backticks, `$((`, here-doc bodies and the `$` before a placeholder. For: keeps the visible line as it is. Against: a shell grammar re-implemented by hand; each round of review found new routes, and `eval` and arithmetic stay open anyway. (c) Ship as VS Code does, with the check as built. The lazy option: known routes stay open. Recommended (a).
- Z280 (2026-10-03 01:10, Axel): (c), VS Code's shape: a LaTeX formatter setting with the choices none, latexindent, tex-fmt and badness, default none, and a path setting per program (four new config keys, approved with this option), built at D14's landing on main; `brew install tex-fmt` so one choice works here. The item as raised: Z280 (2026-10-02, D14's /spec): a LaTeX formatter on this machine. D14 builds Format Document for `.tex` files (Z278) through `tex-fmt`, which is not installed (`command -v tex-fmt` prints nothing; Homebrew offers 0.5.7, MIT). `latexindent` is installed (`/usr/local/texlive/2025/bin/universal-darwin/latexindent`) but stops at once with `Can't locate File/HomeDir.pm in @INC` (TeX Live 2025's script needs a Perl module macOS lacks). What VS Code does (read 2026-10-02 19:30): VS Code itself has no LaTeX formatter (its built-in `latex` extension contributes only `languages` and `grammars`); LaTeX Workshop 10.19.0, installed here, formats through the setting `latex-workshop.formatting.latex` with the choices `none`, `latexindent`, `tex-fmt` and `badness` (the last added in 10.19.0 of 2026-09-17, run as `badness format --stdin-filepath <file> -`; not installed here and not in Homebrew), default `none`, each program found on PATH by default (`latex-workshop.formatting.latexindent.path`, `latex-workshop.formatting.tex-fmt.path`, `latex-workshop.formatting.badness.path`); your VS Code settings set none of these keys, so Format Document on a `.tex` file in your VS Code today changes nothing. Options: (a) I run `brew install tex-fmt` now and D14 stays as briefed, tex-fmt only. For: one command, a single binary, fast; Format Document works at once. Against: one more program on your machine; no choice of formatter, unlike VS Code. (b) I install the Perl module for `latexindent` (`cpan File::HomeDir`, into your user Perl) and D14 is built against `latexindent`. For: the formatter most LaTeX users know, with its own settings files. Against: a Perl module install outside Homebrew. (c) VS Code's shape: a setting for the LaTeX formatter with the choices none, latexindent, tex-fmt and badness, default none as LaTeX Workshop, each program's path a setting too; D14 builds the three programs behind it (added to D14 as a ruling in its repair round, since its builder is building tex-fmt now), and I install tex-fmt so one choice works here. For: the same choice and default as your VS Code with LaTeX Workshop. Against: four new settings keys in the config, the choice and a path per program (a shape you approve with this option); with the default none Format Document does nothing until you pick a program, as in your VS Code today; latexindent still fails here without (b)'s module. (d) neither: Format Document stays unusable here, the lazy option. Recommended (c) with tex-fmt installed: it matches VS Code and leaves the choice of program to you. D14 is built and tested with a stand-in program either way.

- Z143 (raised 2026-10-01 09:39, Axel's question; built in L4, which rewrites the layout tree). The Explorer page's arrangement (`config/layout.yml:82-89`) has an empty right pane, `view: []`, where an opened file lands (`state/workbench/layout/open/landing.ts`). Closing its last tab removes the pane (`removeTab`, `state/workbench/layout/tree.ts:160-166`, which calls `removeNode`), so the left pane takes the whole page and the next opened file splits a new pane off again. Moving the last tab out by drag does the same (`tree.ts:259`). VS Code has one setting for this, `workbench.editor.closeEmptyGroups`, default true; set to false, an empty group stays until closed by hand. VS Code's "Lock Group" is a different thing: it keeps new editors out of a group. (1) A setting `close_empty_panes` in `config/layout.yml`, false by default, shown in Settings. False keeps every pane when its last tab closes or moves out, and Close pane in the pane's menu removes it. For: the one rule VS Code has, a switch for whoever wants the old behaviour, and it fixes the Explorer case. Against: a pane split by hand and emptied stays too, until Close pane. (2) The same rule with no setting: a pane never closes when it empties. For: no new key. Against: no way back to today's behaviour. (3) A per-pane toggle in the pane's menu, "Keep when empty", with the arrangement's `view: []` panes kept from the start. For: only the panes you choose stay. Against: a control VS Code does not have, and one more state saved per pane. (4) Keep only the panes an arrangement declares empty (`view: []`), with no setting or control. For: no new surface. Against: a rule nobody can see; a pane split by hand still closes. (5) One landing pane per page: when a pane's last tab closes or moves out, the pane stays if that tab was a view opened for something (a file, a document, a project) and the page holds no other empty pane; every other pane closes as today, and Close pane removes a kept one. An empty pane already says "Files and documents you open on this page appear here." (`config/text/ui.yml:38`), and the landing rule already sends the next opened view to it (`landing.ts`). For: fixes the Explorer case and the same jump on every page whose document pane the landing rule split off (only the Explorer declares `view: []`, `grep -c` over `config/layout.yml`); hand splits of tool views still clean up; never more than one empty pane. Against: not VS Code's rule; whoever wants every empty pane kept has no switch (the setting of (1) can be added later). Recommendation: (5), changed from (1) after weighing the panes a reader splits and empties by hand, which (1) leaves behind one by one. The lazy option is (4).

What the tree shows: Z105's shape `removed: { at, text }` cannot put the lines back exactly in every undo order. The form editor posts every changed field in one write (`src/lib/views/boards/editor/Editor.svelte:130-137`), so one save can clear `short` and change `title` above it; History offers Undo on every row (`History.svelte:132-138`), so rows can be undone in any order; and a later write elsewhere in the file moves every place after it. The parse check that guards the undo ignores key order and comments, so lines put back at the wrong place still pass it. Second, `at` is already the record's own time (`changes.ts:62-63`, which `undoes` names), so `removed.at` would give one name two meanings in one JSON line.
  - (a) `{ at, text }` as the brief has it, `at` counted in the text just before that field's own edit; when the text no longer fits there, the nearest line start that passes the parse check. For: Z105's shape unchanged. Against: exact only when rows of one save are undone newest first and nothing else changed; after a mixed save or an edit above, the lines can come back above their old neighbour.
  - (b) `{ at, text }` with `at` counted in the text the whole write left. For: exact for undoing the newest row, a mixed save included. Against: two fields cleared in one save are exact only if the lower one is undone first; edits above still move it.
  - (c) `{ offset, text, next }`: `offset` the index (renamed from `at`), `next` the text from the end of the removed span to the end of its line in the file the write left (the whole following line for a whole-line removal, empty at the end of the file). The undo puts the text back just before the occurrence of `next` nearest to `offset`, at a line start for whole lines; only when `next` is not found does it fall to (a)'s nearest line start, and then to today's value write. For: exact in any undo order, after a mixed save and after edits elsewhere, as long as the line that followed is unchanged; one name per meaning. Against: a third key and a renamed one beyond Z105's example; a repeated `next` line is resolved by nearness.
  - (a) is the lazy option. Recommendation: (c).
  - Ruled (c) at 21:30: `removed: { offset, text, next }`, carried into Q111's brief.

Z75 (a) and Z77 (a) fix that the Settings view becomes VS Code's Settings editor over every option from one catalog under `config/catalogs/`; they do not fix the four shapes below, each of which a reader of the config or of the view sees. The tree: the five tracked files hold 66 top-level keys and 249 key paths when a list counts as one value (appearance 6 and 14, behavior 31 and 64, layout 13 and 101, present 1 and 55, sources 15 and 15; counted with `yaml.safe_load` over each file); the Settings view today is `views/system/workbench/Settings.svelte` with `Appearance.svelte`, `RailEditor.svelte` and `PagesReset.svelte`; the only config writes are the rail list, the audit mute list and the deck's lists (`server/edit/writes.ts:109-120`, `deck-edit.ts`); `local.yml`'s keys are `LOCAL_KEYS` (`data/sources/config/local.ts:91`). (1) What one option is. (a) every key path, a list being one option: 249 entries, and `arrangements.<page>.<field>` or `deck.<key>` each get a row, so the editor is long and exact. (b) every top-level key: 66 entries, and `slurm`, `calendar`, `wallpaper` and the like are one row each whose description has to explain every key inside. (c) every key path, except that a family of records of one shape (`themes`, `arrangements`, `collections`, `usage_tiers`, the deck's lists) is one option whose entry describes the record's fields once. Recommended (c): each scalar a reader sets is found by its own name, and a family is explained once instead of once per member. Lazy: (b). (2) The catalog's file and entry. (a) one file `config/catalogs/options.yml`, a map of config file name to a map of dotted key path to `{ description, default, section?, control?, values? }`, `control` one of `toggle`, `number`, `text`, `choice`, `list`, and `values` the choices of a `choice`. (b) one file per config file under `config/catalogs/options/` with the same entries: five shorter files, and a search of descriptions reads five files. (c) the descriptions kept as the YAML comments they are today and parsed out: no second place to write, but a comment is free text with no default or control in it. Recommended (a): Z75 says one catalog, and Z77's check reads one file. Lazy: (c). (3) What Default and Modified mean. (a) the catalog entry holds the default, and Modified is a value in the file that differs from it; the default of a key is then a fact of oculus, the same on every machine. (b) the default is the value at git's HEAD and Modified is an uncommitted change: nothing to write in the catalog, and it says nothing about what the option is set to against oculus's own default. (c) the default is what the code falls back to when the key is absent: only some keys have one, the rest would show none. Recommended (a), and Z77's check then also fails on an entry with no `default`. Lazy: (b). (4) Which options get a control. (a) only what has one today: the appearance values kept per browser and the rail list; every other option shows its value and a control that opens its file at its line. (b) every `toggle`, `number`, `text` and `choice` option gets a control that writes that one key into its config file, comments kept, through one new confirmed write kind `config-key` (`{ file, key, value }`, refused for `local.yml`, for a key with no catalog entry and for a value its `control` does not allow), recorded in the History view and undoable; a `list` or a family opens its file at its line. (c) as (b) without the History record. Recommended (b): an editor that cannot change an option is a list, and the write goes through the chain every other write uses. Lazy: (a). Answer as `Z94 (1) (c), (2) (a), (3) (a), (4) (b)` or "as recommended". Closed 2026-09-30 by Axel: (1) (c), (2) (a), (3) (a), (4) (b).
- Z95, floating panes: three shapes (raised 2026-09-30 at /spec L4; L4 is stopped until ruled). Ruled already: any pane can float over the page with an orange border, on top and still there when the rail switches pages, docked it keeps the border and shows on every page (answer 10, `agents/reviews/axel-2026-09-21.md:63`); the move and resize run on `interactjs` (LA18); Live HPC and Usage are the first floats (Z1); a float's state stands alone so it can move to its own window (Z3). The tree: a page is one tree of splits, panes and page leaves (`state/workbench/layout/model.ts`), saved per browser under `oculus.layout.v1` (`layout/saved/storage.ts`); the Focus arrangement holds Live HPC and Usage as one pane of two tabs (`config/layout.yml:53`); the pane strip's menu holds Open File, the four splits, Close and New Terminal (`shell/panes/pane-view.ts:121-131`); nothing on main floats a pane (`grep -rni float src/lib/shell src/lib/state/workbench` finds two CSS comments, on the Update tray and the palette, and no code). (1) What docked is. (a) a float dragged to the window's left, right or bottom edge becomes a strip along that edge, outside every page's tree, drawn beside whichever page is on screen, resized by a sash, with the orange border; (b) docked is a float dropped into one page's tree, which then shows that pane on the other pages too by putting a copy of the spot in each: every page's arrangement changes when one pane docks; (c) no docking in L4, a float only floats, and docking is a later step. Recommended (a): it is the only reading in which a docked pane is on every page without rewriting every page. Lazy: (c). (2) How a pane floats and comes back. (a) a Float item in the pane strip's right-click menu and in the pane's menu, and a tab dragged off every pane onto the page's middle with Alt held floats on drop; the float's own strip menu holds Dock Left, Dock Right, Dock Bottom and Return to Page, which puts it back in the page on screen as a split of its largest pane; (b) the menu items alone, no drag; (c) a float button on every pane's strip beside the menu. Recommended (a): the menu is where the splits already are, and the drag is how every other pane move is made. Lazy: (b). (3) Where floats are kept and how the first ones are named. (a) the saved layout gains `floats:`, a list beside the pages, each `{ pane, x, y, w, h }` in fractions of the window as split sizes are, or `{ pane, dock: left | right | bottom, size }`; `config/layout.yml` gains a top-level `floats:` list in the same shape with `view:` in place of the pane, which a first load and Reset all pages read; its first entry is `{ view: [hpc, usage], dock: right, size: 0.3 }`, and the Focus arrangement loses its Live HPC and Usage pane; (b) the saved layout alone, no config key: Live HPC and Usage are floated by hand on each browser, and Reset all pages closes every float; (c) as (a) with the first entry floating at the lower right instead of docked. Recommended (a): Z1 names the first floats, so they have to be written somewhere a fresh browser reads, and docked right is where the Focus page has them today. Lazy: (b). Decided in the brief, not asked: the border is a new token `--float-border`, `--c-orange` by default and set by every theme; a float is kept inside the window when the window shrinks; Escape and the keyboard reach a float as they reach a pane. Answer as `Z95 (1) (a), (2) (a), (3) (a)` or "as recommended". Closed 2026-09-30 by Axel: (1) (a), (2) (a), (3) (a).
- Z96, Q85a is too large for one builder (raised 2026-09-30 at /spec Q85a by its brief check, `agents/reviews/Q85a-brief-check.md` section 8; Q85a is stopped until ruled, and Q85b, Q85c and Q85d wait behind it). Z73 (b) made the server one step. The tree: the 80 files with hand checks hold 23,210 lines and 549 check lines (the brief's loop, summed per folder), and `tests/server` with `tests/routes` hold 37,781 lines a builder reads beside them (`find tests/server tests/routes -name '*.ts' | xargs cat | wc -l`). The check lines are decided one by one, since the brief check's probes show zod answering differently from the hand code on a JSON `1e999`, a string that is blank after trimming, `null`, an integer of 2^53 or more, an own `__proto__` key and a query key given twice. By folder, files and check lines: core 5 and 14, root 5 and 22, edit 14 and 189, sessions with transcripts 13 and 105, machine 9 and 79, accounts 13 and 37, files 7 and 40, content 7 and 35, git 7 and 28. `core` goes first in every option, since `core/json.ts` and `core/auth.ts` are what the other folders import. (a) five steps: Q85a1 core and root (10 files, 36 check lines: the request body, the socket message, the hook body), then Q85a2 edit (14, 189), Q85a3 sessions and transcripts (13, 105), Q85a4 machine and accounts (22, 116), Q85a5 files, content and git (21, 103). For: one builder reads each step whole with its tests, and after the first the four have disjoint paths, so three run at once. Against: five briefs, reviews and landings. (b) nine steps, one per folder. For: the smallest reads. Against: four more landings, for folders of 14 to 40 check lines. (c) one step as booked. For: one landing. Against: about 61,000 lines to read before the first edit and no mechanical rule for the 549 lines; the brief check judges that one builder does not finish it in one run with every behaviour held, so it would come back partial. Recommended: (a). Lazy: (c). Decided in the briefs and not asked: a schema stands where a value of type `unknown` is narrowed, wherever it was parsed; every reader keeps answering exactly what it answers on main, the six inputs above included; the transcript's line readers keep `isMap` where a schema costs time (200,000 lines: 1.4 ms against 54 ms in the check's probe). Closed 2026-09-30 by Axel: (a), five steps Q85a1 to Q85a5.

- Z77, a check that every option has a catalog entry (raised 2026-09-30 with Z75 (a), for S3; a new check needs Axel's approval of what it computes). What it would compute, inside `npm run test:checks`: every key path of `config/appearance.yml`, `behavior.yml`, `layout.yml`, `present.yml` and `sources.yml` has an entry in S3's catalog, and every catalog entry names a key one of those files or the server's list of `local.yml` keys holds; `local.yml` itself is never read, its keys come from the list the server checks a save against (HELP.md:234). Options: (a) the check in both directions, failing with the name of each key without an entry and each entry without a key; (b) no check, the catalog kept complete by review; (c) one direction only, keys without an entry. Recommended (a): whether a key has an entry has one answer a machine computes, and without it a key added later shows in the Settings view with no description, which Z75 exists to end; the second direction stops the catalog describing options that are gone. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-30 by Axel: (a); in S3.

Today: the hub and the engine's `config/` folder are fixed roots; `sources.yml` `roots:` adds cathedra and game-engine; `+ root` in the Files header, or Add Folder to Workspace... on a root's right-click, adds a folder typed by path to the current workspace, saved in `~/.oculus/workspaces.json` (`server/files/roots.ts:25-37`, `server/files/fs.ts:158`); the Workspaces section lists the saved workspaces and pressing one switches which added roots are served; "Configured roots" is the name shown for the default workspace, which has no added root, so "Workspaces 1 Configured roots" reads: one workspace, the default. Options: (a) VS Code's model: the Explorer shows the current workspace as a header with its folders as the top-level trees, Add Folder to Workspace and Remove Folder from Workspace on the header's menu and a folder's right-click, a folder picker in place of a typed path, switching workspaces in a picker (VS Code's Open Recent) and not a section of the tree, and the default workspace's folders (the hub, the engine's `config/`, cathedra, game-engine) edited from the page rather than in `sources.yml`; (b) one set of folders and no named workspaces, added and removed from the Explorer; (c) today's model with its labels reworded. Recommended (a): it is VS Code's own model, and every folder is added, removed and switched from the view. (c) is the lazy option. Axel 2026-09-30: leans (a), not locked; he asked what oculus does today that is better than VS Code, so that (a) keeps it. Ruled 2026-09-30 by Axel: (a), with what oculus does today that VS Code does not kept: switching workspaces in place with no reload; the hub and the engine's `config/` folder fixed in every workspace; the Files tab that follows the selected session's workspace; the hidden-files and ignored-files toggles in the header, kept per tab; Bookmarks; scratch Notes; Show in Files from the cards; nothing outside a root served; a root whose folder is gone reported.

- Z69, Q102's Copy as HTML: a library or hand code (raised 2026-09-30 at `/spec` Q102, by the library check `libraries: check` requires). Copy as HTML turns the terminal's buffer, its colours and styles cell by cell, into HTML on the clipboard. xterm's own `@xterm/addon-serialize` does exactly that (`serializeAsHTML()`), and it is what VS Code's Copy as HTML calls. Facts (`npm view`): 0.14.0, MIT, maintained by the xterm.js team (tyriar), released 2025-12-22 in the same wave as the `@xterm/xterm` 6.0.0 oculus runs and the addon-search 0.16 and addon-fit 0.11 it already has; it would replace a hand-written walk over xterm's buffer cells and their attributes; nothing else of Q102 would use it. No ruling names it (`grep -i serialize plan.md` finds none; Q83's ruling covers the search, web-links and unicode11 addons only). The options: (a) `@xterm/addon-serialize` 0.14.0 for Copy as HTML; (b) hand code over xterm's buffer API. Recommendation: (a): it is the addon VS Code uses for this item, from the maintainers of the terminal oculus already runs, and hand code would reimplement its colour and style mapping and carry its own defects; (b) is the lazy option only in the sense of skipping the question, it costs more to write and to prove. Q102 is blocked until the ruling; nothing else is. Ruled 2026-09-30 by Axel: (a), `@xterm/addon-serialize` 0.14.0 for Copy as HTML.
- Z70, Q88b's two pane-strip settings: their config keys (raised 2026-09-30 at `/spec` Q88b). Q88b's line asks for "the Tab Bar and Editor Actions Position settings" on the pane strip's right-click menu (the inventory, `agents/reviews/vscode-parity.md:269`). VS Code's are `workbench.editor.showTabs` (`multiple`, `single`, `none`: every tab, only the active one, no strip) and `workbench.editor.editorActionsLocation` (`default`, `titleBar`, `hidden`: the pane's action buttons on the strip, in the title bar, or not drawn). oculus has neither: `config/appearance.yml` holds no tab or action key (`grep -n "tab\|action" config/appearance.yml` prints nothing), and X3c will add `wrap_tabs: false` there (Z47 3 (a)). A key and its values are a user-visible shape, so the brief cannot take them. The options: (a) two keys in `config/appearance.yml` beside `wrap_tabs`, `show_tabs: multiple | single | none` (default `multiple`) and `editor_actions: strip | hidden` (default `strip`; oculus has no title bar, so VS Code's `titleBar` has no place), each with a control in the Settings view's Appearance section as `wrap_tabs` gets, the menu's two items setting them; (b) the two settings move to X3c, which owns the tab strip and its `wrap_tabs` key, and Q88b builds the rest of its line; (c) the two items are left out of oculus. Recommendation: (a): it is what the ruled line asks, the keys sit with the tab key X3c adds and follow VS Code's values, and the rest of Q88b does not wait on X3c; (b) splits one menu's items across two steps for no gain beyond sequencing; (c) is the lazy option, it drops two items Axel's Z52 (b) put in scope. Q88b is blocked until the ruling; nothing else is. Ruled 2026-09-30 by Axel: (a), `show_tabs: multiple | single | none` (default `multiple`) and `editor_actions: strip | hidden` (default `strip`) in `config/appearance.yml`, each with a control in the Settings view's Appearance section, the pane strip menu's two items setting them.

- Z52, which of VS Code's right-click menu items Q88 builds (raised 2026-09-29 at /spec Q88). The inventory from VS Code's source (Z51 (c)) is in `agents/reviews/vscode-parity.md`, section "Right-click menus (owner Q88)", every item with its condition and oculus's side. About half the items run on an action oculus has (open, open beside, stage, unstage, discard, the stage and discard alls, open changes, reveal in the Files view, add and remove a root, download, kill, split, new terminal, close a pane, copy commit id and message) or need only the clipboard (copy path, copy relative path, cut, copy and paste in a preview or a text box, select all). The rest need a capability oculus lacks: in the Files view, New File, New Folder, Rename, Delete, Cut, Copy and Paste of files and folders, and Upload, each a write to the reader's disk through a new server route; Select for Compare and Compare Selected (a diff of two chosen files); in Source Control, Add to .gitignore and Cherry Pick; in the terminal, Rename, Change Icon, Change Color, Clear and Copy as HTML; on the pane's strip, a New Text File and the Tab Bar and Editor Actions Position settings. Items with no oculus counterpart (Timeline, Tests, Chat, Share, extensions, a second window, dictation) are left out in every option. Options:
  - (a) Q88 builds every item, the new capabilities included, in one step: the menus on every surface and the server routes for the file writes (Delete moving to the macOS Trash, as VS Code does where a trash exists), the two-file compare, the `.gitignore` write, cherry-pick, and the terminal's name, icon and colour. Until tmux has answered the server's first `list-sessions` (just after a server start, or when that first read times out), the server has no list, and today it sends an empty one, which the page would read as every terminal having ended and close every Terminal tab while the terminals run on. The message between the server and the page is a wire format, so its shape is yours to rule. Options:
  - (a) As built: `terminals` is left out of the message until tmux has answered once, and a page reads a message without it as saying nothing about any terminal. Pros: the smallest change; the page's reading needs no new field; an old page and a new server still agree. Cons: one field of the message becomes optional, so every reader must handle its absence. Recommended.
  - (b) `terminals` always present, plus a field `terminalsRead: boolean` that says whether tmux has answered. Pros: no optional field. Cons: two fields to keep in step, and a reader that forgets the flag makes the same mistake as today.
  - (c) The server sends no `sessions` message at all until tmux has answered. Pros: no shape change. Cons: the Sessions list of Claude and Codex sessions waits on tmux at every start, and waits for good when tmux does not answer.

So one terminal is both a tab somewhere and a row in each Terminal tab's list: two ways to the same thing, mixing VS Code's terminal panel (one panel, a list of terminals on its right, New terminal adds a row) with VS Code's terminal in the editor area (a tab per terminal, no list). Options:
  - (a) The panel: one Terminal tab holds every terminal; its list switches the terminal the tab shows; New terminal adds a row to this tab and shows it; Split divides this tab's body between two terminals, as VS Code's split does; a terminal is no longer a tab of its own, and the pin goes. Pros: one place for terminals, as Q89 set out to draw VS Code's terminal panel. Cons: two terminals side by side in different panes of a page are no longer possible outside Split.
  - (b) The editor tab: every terminal is a tab of its own, the list goes, New terminal opens a tab in the pane it was pressed in. Pros: panes place terminals freely. Cons: no list of terminals beside them; the Sessions view is the overview.
  - (c) Keep both. This is the lazy option.
  - (d) Each Terminal tab is a terminal panel of its own (Axel's question, 2026-09-28): a tab owns one or more terminals, its list shows only those, New terminal in a tab adds to that tab, Split divides that tab's body, a terminal belongs to exactly one tab, and the Sessions view lists every terminal; pressing one there shows the tab that owns it, and a terminal no tab owns (started by a task, a hook or LaTeX, or left when its tab closed) is taken into the Terminal tab of the page on screen, or a new one. A tab closes when its last terminal ends; closing a tab leaves its terminals running, listed in Sessions. Pros: no terminal is shown in two places, terminals still sit in any pane of any page, the list stays short. Cons: ownership kept per tab and pruned as terminals end, the following-the-selection tab and the page-wide order go, and adoption rules for unowned terminals. This is the Windows Terminal and iTerm model (tabs, each holding its panes) with VS Code's panel inside each tab.

- Z8, Q77a's browser half (raised 2026-09-27 by Q77a's premise checks). Q77a as ruled proves a unit directive in memory in one runner process per test file, and a browser directive on a development server that reloads the one changed file. Measured on main at load 5 to 8: a unit directive today costs a copy of the tree (1.2 s) and a Vitest start (1.6 to 2.9 s); in one Vitest process through its Node API with the reverted text served by a Vite load hook, the same case ran green, red under its revert, green, red, at 0.18 to 0.45 s each (`scratchpad/rc-probe.mjs`). 1,429 of the tree's 1,763 directives are unit directives. A browser directive today costs a build (8.9 s) and a Playwright run with its own server (4.6 to 13.1 s). On a development server started for the run (a scratch copy whose browser layer serves `vite dev`), a spec ran in 9.7 to 11.5 s; on one kept running, 3.0 to 7.2 s, and a client-side revert written into the copy turned its case red with no restart. But a server kept running keeps the hub the last run wrote, so a red is trusted only when the case also passes before and after the revert on that server: three runs, about 15 to 22 s, the same as today. The server context (watchers, socket, terminals) is built once at startup from modules Node imports (`src/lib/server/root/vite-plugin.ts`), so the 27 browser directives on server code, config and the layer's helpers would keep today's path in any case. Options: (a) Q77a builds the unit half as ruled (one Vitest process per test file, the revert served in memory, today's copy as the fallback when the in-memory run stays green or does not run, for a target a case starts as a process or reads from disk) and browser directives keep today's copy and build; (b) Q77a also serves browser directives from a development server kept per spec file, each red confirmed by a run before and after, measured at about today's cost; (c) a development server started per browser directive, about 11 s against about 14 to 20 s today, with the Vite dependency cache of the copy kept between starts. Recommended (a): it removes about 3.5 s from each of 1,429 directives, and (b) and (c) add a second serving path for the browser layer for a saving the measurement does not show. (a) is also the cheapest to build, which is the lazy option's mark; it is recommended on the measurement, since the browser work of (b) and (c) buys no time. Q77a is not dispatched before this ruling. Closed 2026-09-27, Axel: "Z8 (a)"; Q77a builds the unit half, and browser directives keep today's copy and build.

- L2, the source editor and the Source Control diff (raised 2026-09-26 by Axel's question; the audit's report on `views/sources/` adds detail). Today the editor is a text area with `highlight.js` colouring laid over it (`src/lib/views/sources/source/`, Editor.svelte 410 lines, Code.svelte 132, with Gutter and Preview), and X3b builds the diff, word diff and merge editor by hand. (a) Monaco 0.57.0: MIT, Microsoft, released 2026-09-24; VS Code's own editor, so its editing (multi-cursor, find and replace, folding, bracket matching, undo history, the minimap, its keybindings) and its diff editor, side by side and inline, are VS Code's; themes are defined in its own API from colour values, so oculus's tokens are read and a Monaco theme redefined at every theme change; it runs language workers that Vite must be set up to bundle; its API is imperative and is wrapped in one Svelte component. (b) CodeMirror 6 (`codemirror` 6.0.2 with `@codemirror/view` 6.43.13, released 2026-09-22, and `@codemirror/merge` 6.12.2 for side-by-side and unified diffs): MIT, Marijn Haverbeke; themed through CSS, so oculus's tokens apply directly as CSS variables; modular, one package per feature and language; its behaviour and keybindings are its own, close to but not VS Code's. (c) Keep the hand-built editor and diff. Neither library ships a three-way merge editor like VS Code's (not verified against their documentation yet; the audit checks it), so the merge editor stays oculus's in (a) and (b). Recommended (a) Monaco: your standing demand is that VS Code surfaces match VS Code exhaustively, and Monaco is that editor and that diff, where CodeMirror would be a close copy that still needs parity work; the cost of (a) is the theme mapping and the worker setup, both one-time. (b) wins on theming and fits Svelte more naturally. (c) keeps the most code and the furthest from VS Code. Checked since: Monaco's public API (`esm/vs/editor/editor.api.d.ts` of 0.57.0) has `createDiffEditor` and no merge editor, and `@codemirror/merge` 6.12.2's `MergeView` takes two documents, `a` and `b`; neither has a three-way merge editor. Closed 2026-09-26, Axel: (a) Monaco, for the source editor and the Source Control diff; the step that brings it in is booked after the audit is ruled. The lazy option was (c), keeping the hand-built editor and diff.
- Q76, the `file` field on the `api/docs` answer (raised 2026-09-26 by Q76's report, judgment call 1, and its review): every answer of `api/docs`, the 200 and the 404 for a missing file, now carries `file`, the absolute path of the file it read. The document store needs it to tell whether a `files` message's root holds a document; the manual's path is known only to the server. The page already receives every absolute root in the `files` and `git` payloads and every manifest's absolute path in the snapshot, so the field adds the engine directory's path and nothing of a new kind; a path that climbs out of its root gets no `file`. A wire shape is yours to see. Recommended: keep it. The alternative, the server naming the watched root that holds each document, puts the root lookup of the watcher into the document route and still sends an absolute root; the lazy option would be to drop the field and re-read every document on every message, which is the flicker's cause. Closed 2026-09-26, Axel: keep. Neither option was the lazy one; they differ only in request count (the flicker's fix is the held answer and the 304, not the field).

- S2, a new form in `config/layout.yml` (raised 2026-09-26 by S2's review). S2's Sessions page puts a Files tab beside Changes that follows the selected session's workspace. The Files view knows that mode only from its instance state, and an arrangement in `config/layout.yml` names a tab by its view alone (`{ kind: pane, view: [changes, files] }`), so the builder added a second tab form, `{ view: files, state: { follow: true } }`, read by `state/workbench/navigation/arrangement.ts`. Options: (a) keep that form: any tab of any arrangement may carry a starting `state:`, checked by the view's own reader; (b) no new form: the Files tab on the Sessions page starts plain, and the reader turns on Follow once from the tab's toolbar, which the tab then keeps. Recommended (a): the page works as the three columns you asked for from its first open, and the form is general rather than a special case for one view; (b) leaves the layout file's vocabulary as it is but makes the page wrong until a press. Ruled 2026-09-26, Axel: (a), as recommended.
- Q67, two shapes its builder took (raised 2026-09-26 by Q67's review). (1) The Personal group's keyboard letter. Q67 adds the Account setup view to the Personal group, which then holds five entries (Memories, Calendar, Account setup and the group's two documents), and `config/layout.yml:25` rules that a group of more than four entries is reached only by its own chord. So Personal needs a letter: Memories, Calendar, Account setup and the two documents become `p1` to `p5`. Before, Memories, Calendar and the two documents were the 12th to 15th entries of the `v` list, and only the first nine get a key (`state/workbench/navigation/catalogue.ts:155`, `at < 9`), so they had no key; the chord gives them keys and takes none away. The letters in use are `m`, `c`, `s`, `y` and `v` (`grep -n "chord:" config/layout.yml`). Options: (a) `p` for Personal, as the builder chose, with the group glyph `memories`; (b) another free letter you name. Recommended (a): `p` is free and is the group's first letter, as `s` and `c` are for theirs. (2) A new `local.yml` key, `open_bin`: the program an `https` address (a consent page, an event's link) is handed to, `/usr/bin/open` when absent (`server/files/open.ts:56, 280-288`). The builder added it so the browser suite's served test engine records the consent address instead of opening a real browser; the calendar and mail links go through the same opener. Options: (a) keep `open_bin` in `local.yml`, as `claude_bin` names the Claude command there; (b) a server flag `--open-bin <program>` beside `--engine`, so `local.yml` keeps no key a reader would never set; (c) neither, and the browser suite never presses Connect or Add, leaving the consent start proven only by the node tests. Recommended (a): the test engine is configured the way a machine is, through its own `local.yml`, as `claude_bin` already is; (c) drops proof and is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-26, Axel: (1) (a) and (2) (a), as recommended.

- X3a, three shapes of the Explorer (raised 2026-09-25 by X3a's spec). (1) The file icons. Today every file draws one of three lucide icons (`glyphOf`, `views/sources/files/tree/Tree.svelte:74-80`) and nothing maps an extension to an icon (`LANGUAGES`, `state/sources/fs.ts:86-103`, maps to highlighter languages only). Options: (a) the Seti icon set, the source VS Code's default file icon theme is built from (`seti-ui` 1.11.0, MIT, `npm view seti-ui`; that VS Code builds from it is not verified in this turn), with its own extension and name table and colours; (b) lucide's `file-*` icons, coloured per language, from a new catalog `config/catalogs/file-icons.yml`. Recommended (a): the tree then reads as VS Code's, and the table comes with the set rather than being written by hand. (2) File nesting (VS Code's `explorer.fileNesting`, off by default there): options (a) the patterns in a new catalog `config/catalogs/file-nesting.yml` seeded with VS Code's defaults, nesting switched on and off per Files tab; (b) no nesting. Recommended (a); (b) drops a row of the inventory and is the lazy option. (3) The Timeline section's local saves: source-tab saves are logged nowhere today (`grep -n logChanges src/lib/server/files/source.ts` finds nothing). Options: (a) a copy of the file before each save under `~/.oculus/history/`, kept to VS Code's defaults (50 per file, files over 256 KB not kept), shown in the Timeline beside the file's commits (`git log -- <path>`, a read-only form added to DESIGN.md's list) with compare and restore; (b) commits only. Recommended (a); (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-25, Axel: (1) (a), (2) (a), (3) (a), as recommended.

- X3c, two shapes of the tab strip (raised 2026-09-25 by X3c's spec). (1) Pinned tabs: the saved layout's `Instance` has `preview?: true` and no pin (`state/workbench/layout/model.ts:18`; "pinned" today means a view held to one session, `layout/instances.ts:98-117`). Options: (a) `pinned?: true` on `Instance` beside `preview`, the layout version raised from 4 with a migration, a pinned tab drawn first with a pin in place of its close control and kept by Close Others and Close All, as VS Code does; (b) no pinned tabs. Recommended (a); (b) is the lazy option. (2) Wrapped tabs (VS Code's `workbench.editor.wrapTabs`): options (a) a toggle in the pane menu kept per browser in the UI store, as the hidden status items are; (b) a key in `config/behavior.yml`. Recommended (a): it is a preference of the screen, not of the hub, and follows Axel's ruling for the status items. Ruled 2026-09-25, Axel: (1) (a), (2) (a), as recommended.

- S2, where the composer's choices live (raised 2026-09-25 by S2's spec). S2 builds VS Code's composer for a new session: workspace, agent (Claude, Codex, shell), account, model, effort and permission mode, then a prompt. Today oculus starts a bare `claude` or `codex` with no flag (`server/machine/pty/sessions.ts:131-136`, `commandFor`), and no file names the choices: `grep -rn -- '--effort\|--permission-mode' src` finds nothing, and the only model key is `chat.model: "opus"` (`config/behavior.yml:86`). The CLIs take: Claude `--model <alias or name>`, `--effort low|medium|high|xhigh|max`, `--permission-mode acceptEdits|auto|bypassPermissions|manual|dontAsk|plan`; Codex `-m <model>`, `-c model_reasoning_effort=...`, `-s read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access` and `-a <approval>` (`claude --help`, `codex --help`, Claude Code 2.1.282, codex-cli 0.155.1). Options: (a) a new catalog `config/catalogs/agents.yml`, one entry per agent listing its models, efforts and permission modes, each with the words the picker shows and the flag it passes, and a `default:` per list; the composer remembers the last choice per tab in instance state; a CLI release that adds a value is one line in that file; (b) no file: the lists read from each CLI's `--help` text at server start, the defaults the CLI's own. Recommended (a): the lists are what Axel picks from, so they are his to trim or reorder, and a parse of help text breaks silently on the next CLI release. The worktree toggle and the branch stay with A2 (its ruling puts the worktree under `.agents/worktrees/<name>`, which `claude -w` does not); S2 shows the workspace's branch read-only. Quick chats are left out, as P1's inventory says, the terminal being the chat. Ruled 2026-09-25, Axel: (a), as recommended.

- The layers diagram's form (raised 2026-09-24, from Axel's question about the diagrams). `docs/diagrams/layers.svg` draws 61 folders and 372 import edges in one picture, 6,640 by 1,315 px, and cannot be read at any zoom: every folder imports several others, so the edges cross the whole width. Options: (a) an overview of the layers alone (data, server, state, ui, shell, views, routes), one arrow per pair with its import count, plus one diagram per layer showing its folders and what each reaches outside the layer; (b) keep one picture but draw only the imports that cross a layer, with counts, and leave the folders inside a layer unjoined. Recommended (a): it answers both questions a reader brings, how the layers stand and what one folder depends on, and each picture stays small; (b) still draws 242 crossing edges between folders (58 from views to state alone). Neither is the lazy option; keeping the picture as it is would be. Closed 2026-09-24, Axel: (a), an overview of the layers and one diagram per layer; folded into Q71.

- U1, the `glyph:` key on each theme row of `config/appearance.yml` (raised 2026-09-24 at U1's review; asked in chat the same day). The key names the icon drawn beside a theme in the Settings theme menu; a missing or unknown one is a finding and the entry is drawn with its words alone. Options: (a) keep the key, one line per theme, so each theme can carry its own icon; (b) no key: one fixed icon for the ordinary themes and another for the terminal themes, as the old characters did. Recommended (a): an icon per theme is a choice of the reader's, and the findings already hold it. (b) is the lazy option only in that it adds nothing. Closed 2026-09-24, Axel: (a), keep the key; (b) was the lazy option.
- L6, which events post a notification (raised 2026-09-24 by L6's brief). L6 builds the bell, the notification centre, the toasts and Do Not Disturb as VS Code draws them, and moves the rail's refusal line into a notification; nothing else in oculus posts one yet. Options: (a) also post (1) a session that starts waiting for input, with an Open action, (2) an update ready in the update tray, with Open, (3) a Live HPC job that leaves the queue, finished or failed, with Open, and (4) a write the server refuses, beside the line the view already draws; (b) the refusal alone, each further source ruled one at a time later. Recommended (a): these are the four events oculus already knows of that happen while the reader looks elsewhere, which is what a notification is for in VS Code, and each is one post through the store L6 builds. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled before L6's repair round, the sources go into that round; otherwise they are a step of their own. Closed 2026-09-24, Axel: (a), all four sources as well as the refusal; (b) was the lazy option. Sent to L6's builder while it runs, so they are built in its first run.
- The Views catalogue and the Views and Settings page itself (raised 2026-09-23 by Axel: "Views and Settings are nice, but I seemingly cannot add any views to this page? As it always add to the previous page"). As ruled, a press opens on the page the reader came from. Options: (a) a catalogue entry dragged onto a pane of the page on screen opens there, as a tab dragged onto a pane does, and each entry's context menu offers "Open on this page" and "Open beside on this page"; a plain press stays as ruled; (b) a modifier (Alt-press) opens on the page on screen. Recommended (a): it is the way VS Code places a view where it is dropped, and a hidden modifier is found by nobody. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), as recommended; built in L5.
- Q67, how much of a calendar or mail account's setup is automated (raised 2026-09-23 by Axel). Today each account needs a `local.yml` row written by hand, a credential file per account holding a provider app's client half, and a Connect press. What only the provider's own console can make is the app itself: a Google "Desktop app" OAuth client, or a Microsoft Entra public-client registration; neither `az` nor `gcloud` is installed here (`which az gcloud`: not found), so neither can be scripted today. Options: (a) an Add account control in the Calendar and Inbox views: pick Google or Microsoft and type a label, and oculus writes the `local.yml` row and the credential file itself and starts Connect at once; the provider app is set up once per provider, not per account, on a setup page that walks through the console step by step with a link to each console page, the exact redirect addresses to paste and one field for the client id (and the Google secret), and that one app then serves every account of that provider and both the Calendar and the Inbox, each consent still separate; (b) as (a), and oculus also registers the Microsoft app itself through the Azure CLI when it is installed and signed in, the reader asked first before it is installed with Homebrew; (c) documentation only. Recommended (a): it turns every account after the first into a label and a consent, with nothing typed into files; (b) adds an install and a tenant login for a step done once. (c) is the lazy option. Not verified: whether an unpublished Google app must list each Google account as a test user, and whether UHasselt's and UTwente's tenants let a user approve an app; the setup page would say what each console asks for. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), as recommended.
- A1, how a review comment reaches a session (raised 2026-09-23 when A1 was booked). oculus can type into a terminal it started, through tmux (`server/machine/pty/sessions.ts:8`, `send-keys -l`), but not into a session running in a terminal of its own, such as this orchestrating session. Options: (a) the comment, prefixed with the file and line it is on, is typed into the session's oculus terminal when the session runs in one, and for any other session it is copied to the clipboard with a line saying so; (b) the comment control is offered only for sessions running in an oculus terminal. Recommended (a): every session can be commented on, and the one route oculus cannot take is said plainly. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), as recommended.
- A2, the worktree a new session starts in (raised 2026-09-23 when A2 was booked). Options: (a) under the repository's `.agents/worktrees/<name>`, the convention this hub's plans already use, on a local branch of the same name that lives only as long as the worktree, removed from the Repositories view's Worktrees section behind a confirmation that names any uncommitted change; (b) in a folder oculus keeps under `~/.oculus/worktrees/`. Recommended (a): one place for every worktree of a repository, and the hub's rule that a worktree's branch lives only as long as the worktree already fits it. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), as recommended.
- A3, where a schedule is written and what happens to a missed run (raised 2026-09-23 when A3 was booked). oculus runs only while its server does, so a schedule fires only then. Options: (a) a `schedule:` field per task under `tasks:` in `config/behavior.yml` (hourly, daily at a time, or weekly on a day at a time), a run missed while the server was down runs once when it starts again, and the Update tray shows each task's next run; (b) the same field, and a missed run is skipped. Recommended (a): a daily feed update that fell during a closed laptop still happens that day. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), as recommended.
- L5, the BOOKMARKS group in a 48 px rail (raised 2026-09-23 at L5's premise check). An icon-only rail about 48 px wide cannot hold a bookmark's name, and every bookmark draws the same file icon, so the group as it is becomes a column of identical icons told apart only by hovering. Options: (a) one Bookmarks icon at the rail's foot, beside Search and Update, opening a menu of the bookmarks by name, as VS Code puts its account and manage menus there; (b) each bookmark an icon-only button with its name as the tooltip; (c) the bookmarks leave the rail and live in the Files view only, where they already are. Recommended (a): every bookmark stays one click and one read away, and the rail stays a column of page icons. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), one Bookmarks icon at the rail's foot opening a menu of the bookmarks by name.
- L5, the rail drawn like VS Code's activity bar (raised 2026-09-23 by Axel after L3: "The badges with the numbers in the rail are UGLY. They are kinda floating outside the fucking buttons. Also, compared to vscode, the buttons in the rail themselves are UGLY."). Two shapes. (1) The button: (a) icon only, about 48 px wide, muted until hovered, the page on screen in full colour with a 2 px accent bar on its left edge, the name as the tooltip, as VS Code draws it; (b) the icon with its name under it, restyled flat without the boxed border. Recommended (a): it is the look asked for, and the names are on the tooltip and in the Pages view. (2) The badge: VS Code draws one small filled count on the icon's lower right corner, inside the button. (a) one badge per button, the count of the first view of the page that has one, drawn that way, the other views' counts on their tabs; (b) every view's count, as ruled on 2026-09-23, drawn as a stack on the icon; (c) no count, a dot on the icon when any view of the page has one. Recommended (a): one number fits a 48 px button, and it keeps the most-watched count (Projects 52, Leads, the audit) in view. (b) is the lazy option, since it keeps what was called ugly. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (1)(a) and (2)(a), as recommended.
- U1, as little unicode in oculus as possible (raised 2026-09-23 by Axel: "I would prefer actual icons instead of weird unicode. In fact, I would like to get the entirety of oculus to be as little unicode as possible."). Measured: every one of the 137 glyph names already maps to a line icon (`config/catalogs/icons.yml`); unicode still reaches the page through 11 `{G.name}` tokens in 5 text files (filled in as characters by `resolveGlyphTokens`, `state/words/text.ts:70`), the venue ribbon's sparkline (block characters, `views/sources/venues/Ribbon.svelte:17`), a mark badge's hover words (`views/registry.ts:98`), and the character column of `config/catalogs/glyphs.yml`, the fallback the terminal themes swap for ASCII. Options: (a) every glyph is drawn as its icon everywhere: a text carrying a glyph token draws the icon inline, the sparkline is drawn as SVG bars, a mark badge's hover says its meaning in words, and `glyphs.yml` loses its unicode column, keeping each name with its ASCII stand-in for the terminal themes, so an unknown icon is an error rather than a character; (b) the same drawing changes, with `glyphs.yml`'s characters kept as the fallback. Recommended (a): it leaves no unicode in the shipped vocabulary and no route by which a character can reach the page. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), as recommended. Corrected at U1's premise check: the tokens are 28 in 6 files, the 11 in `config/text/` and 17 theme labels in `config/appearance.yml` (13 `{G.theme_rice}`, 4 `{G.theme_base}`), which draw the characters of the Settings theme menu.
- The order of L5 and U1 (raised 2026-09-23). Recommended: L5 and U1 before L4, since L4's floating panes are drawn in the shell L5 restyles, and U1 touches every surface L4 would add to. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: L5 and U1 before L4, as recommended; the pause is lifted for L5 and U1, one at a time, since U1 changes a configuration file.
- L3, the rail buttons' badges (raised 2026-09-23 by L3's review, `agents/reviews/L3-refuter.md`, Spec 4). The rail used to draw each view's live count (Projects 52, Coauthor 16, Archive 25, the sessions waiting count); now a rail button is a page and draws none, and the counts show only on the pane's tabs and in the Views catalogue. Options: (a) a page button draws the badges of the views its page holds, in the order of its tabs, the way a tab draws its own; (b) the rail stays plain and the counts live on the tabs and in the catalogue. Recommended (a): the rail is the one surface always on screen, and a waiting session or a new lead is what it was there to show. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), a page button draws the badges of the views its page holds; sent into L3's repair round 1.
- L3, where the Views catalogue opens a view (raised 2026-09-23 by L3's review, Spec 6). Your ruling reads "a catalogue of every view, opened into the current page from there". As built, a press opens the view into the Views and Settings page itself, next to the catalogue. Options: (a) into the page the reader was on before switching to Views and Settings, and that page is shown; (b) into the Views and Settings page, as built. Recommended (a): a view opened beside the catalogue has to be moved by hand to where it is wanted, and the catalogue exists to fill the reader's own pages. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), into the page the reader was on before, which is then shown; sent into L3's repair round 1.
- O31's launch note from the plan skills (raised 2026-09-23 at O31's landing). The brief planned to change the plan-orchestration skill's launch recipes at landing to call oculus's `bin/dispatch-note.mjs`, but the plan skills name no project ("It carries no project name and no vendor name; those are in `.agents/plan.yaml`"), so they cannot call an oculus path: two rules clash. Options: (a) an optional key in `.agents/plan.yaml`, `launch_note:`, holding the command that records a launch (here `node tools/oculus/bin/dispatch-note.mjs`), which the launch recipes run at start, when the transcript is known and at the end, and skip when the key is empty; (b) leave the recipes as they are, so only a launcher that calls the script by hand records its builder. Recommended (a): it is the plan skills' own way to carry a project specific, and a Codex worker launched by the loop is the case the note exists for. (b) is the lazy option. Tonight's builders are Claude agents of this session, which the Agents view already draws, so nothing waits on it tonight. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), the optional `launch_note:` key in `.agents/plan.yaml`, run by the launch recipes; booked as O32.
- O31, a launched builder whose launcher dies before `end` (raised 2026-09-23 by O31's review, `agents/reviews/O31-refuter.md`, Spec 3). When the builder's own transcript is known, its row follows that session's own liveness, which the repair round builds. When no transcript was ever recorded, nothing in the ruled record says whether the builder still runs, so its row reads `running` for good. Options: (a) add the builder's process id to the record (`--pid` on `start`, checked the way `sessions/registry.ts` checks a registry pid), so a launch with no transcript is known dead once its process is; (b) leave the record as ruled, and a launch with no transcript and no `end` reads `running` until someone ends it. Recommended (a): the row otherwise tells the reader something false, and a pid is the one fact that answers it; it is one optional field and the writer already runs where the launcher knows the child's pid. (b) is the lazy option. O31 lands without it either way; (a) would be a small step of its own. Found at O31's landing: (a) also closes the one case the landing's rule leaves, a Codex launcher with a Codex builder, whose rows read done once both rollouts have been silent for two minutes. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), the builder's process id in the record; booked as O32.
- Q65, the work a hidden tab keeps doing (raised 2026-09-23 by Q65's review, `agents/reviews/Q65-refuter.md`, Behaviour). A pane now keeps every tab it has shown mounted, and a hidden tab does the same work as a shown one. Measured over one minute each on the served build (Q65-report.md, round 1, item 9): a hidden Files tab with four folders open re-read every open folder on one bookmark write, 9 requests, 0.42 to 0.44 s of server CPU and 4 `check-ignore` runs, the same as shown; a hidden Transcript following a line every 5 s made 24 requests and 25 socket frames and 127 ms of page work, against 211 ms shown. A running Terminal hidden is not measured, since the served test layer has no tmux. Repeated listings of one folder by several Files tabs within two seconds now share one `check-ignore` run (fixed at Q65's landing). Options: (a) a hidden tab defers its re-reads and its follow until it is shown again, and then catches up once, while a Terminal keeps its stream so no output is lost; (b) a hidden tab keeps working as a shown one does. Recommended (a): the work of a hidden tab has no reader, and its cost grows with every tab a reader has opened; (a) is a step of its own, since it touches the store and every view that follows. (b) is the lazy option. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), a hidden tab defers its re-reads and its follow until shown, a Terminal keeping its stream; booked as Q66.
- L3, three shapes of the rail's pages no ruling names (raised 2026-09-23 at L3's premise check; the scope in `agents/briefs/L3.md`). (1) The rail list in `config/layout.yml`: (a) a list `rail:` of `{ label, glyph, page }`, where `page` names a key of `arrangements:` and each rail page's first arrangement is written there in the node shape `arrangements:` already uses (the Sessions arrangement becomes the Sessions page as it is); (b) the same list with each page's tree written inside its own entry. Recommended (a): one node shape in one place, and the list stays one line per button. (2) What the rail no longer draws: `nav_groups` with their chords `c`, `m`, `s`, `y`, `direct_chord: v`, and the three `docs:` entries (Research approach, Agent approach, HPC how-to): (a) kept as the headings of the view catalogue on the Views and Settings page, a chord and a digit still opening a view, and the docs listed in that catalogue under their group; (b) removed with the rail's groups. Recommended (a): nothing a reader reaches today becomes unreachable and the keys keep working. (3) The page keys: the digits 1 to 9 switch pages, and Ctrl+Shift+Left and Right move the page in the strip (DESIGN.md "Pages"). (a) the digits switch to the rail's pages in rail order and the move keys go, since the order is the rail list edited in Settings; (b) the digits keep switching every page in the order made. Recommended (a): the rail is the only place pages are listed once the strip is gone. The bookmark merge needs no ruling: a Files bookmark of an `.html` file already opens in the document view (`views/sources/files/opening.ts:58`), so the two `layout.yml` bookmarks move into the bookmarks file. The lazy option in each: (2)(b), which drops what it does not want to place. Ruled 2026-09-23, Axel: (1)(a), (2)(a), (3)(a).
- O31, how a builder on the other harness becomes visible in oculus (raised 2026-09-23 by `/spec oculus/migration O31`; no brief, no worktree and no dispatch exist for O31 until it is ruled). A Claude builder is already drawn: it is a native agent of the orchestrating session, and the Agents view lists the subagents a session dispatched (`src/lib/views/sessions/agents/Agents.svelte`). A Codex builder is a separate process and appears nowhere under its orchestrator. The plan names two mechanisms that disagree: the booking of 2026-09-11 (`agents/briefs/O31.md`) has the orchestrator write a dispatch note to `~/.oculus/dispatches.json` at every launch, and the plan line of 2026-09-21 says the sessions views draw the worker "from the dispatch block" of the ledger. Options: (a) the dispatch note: one JSON record per launch in `~/.oculus/dispatches.json` (step, worktree, harness and model, the orchestrating session's id, the worker's transcript or rollout path, launch and exit times), written by the plan-orchestration skill's launch step, so the Ordo skills change too, and read by oculus's sessions layer; (b) oculus reads each plan's `orchestrator-state.md` dispatch block, which needs a new `local.yml` key naming where the ledgers are and a reader for the block's YAML inside Markdown; (c) drop the worker part and keep O31 as the account folders alone, since the default builder is `claude:opus` and is already visible. Recommended (a): one small machine-local file like the others under `~/.oculus`, it works for any plan in any repository, and oculus parses no ledger Markdown. (c) is the lazy option: it costs least and leaves a Codex builder, which the configuration still allows per brief, invisible. Also for the ruling: O31's other half, the three session stores read from `local.yml`'s `accounts`, is specified in full in its brief and writes no file Q65 writes, so it can run beside Q65 now while the worker half waits; recommended. Closed 2026-09-23, Axel: (a), and the account folders run now; he added that other skills, which may or may not launch agents, can also run, so the note is written by one script any launcher calls and is safe when several write at once. The lazy option was (c).

- D16, how a file reaches its program (raised 2026-09-16 16:47 by D16's third review, `agents/reviews/D16-refuter3.md`): the allow list holds for the names, aliases in the bookmark format, symlinks, execute bits and Unicode tricks, but macOS `open <file>` lets Launch Services choose the program, and the review found it chooses past the list without anything being opened: a listed `report.docx` carrying a `com.apple.LaunchServices.OpenWith` extended attribute naming Python Launcher or Terminal is handed to that program (200, opener called); a file flagged as an alias in its Finder info with an empty data fork passes; a `report.docx` symlink to a folder opens; 26 folder suffixes macOS itself calls packages (`.xcodeproj`, `.swiftpm`, `.playground`, `.service`, `.osax` and others) are not on the refusal list; the server keeps the list read at start while the page follows a config edit. Options inside the rules: (a) name the program: `open.program_ext` becomes a map from extension to the application's bundle id (for example `.docx: com.microsoft.Word`, `.xlsx: com.microsoft.Excel`, `.pptx: com.microsoft.Powerpoint`, `.pages: com.apple.iWork.Pages`), the server runs `open -b <id> <file>` so no per-file override or Launch Services choice redirects it, an extension with no id is not offered; a folder is shown in Finder with `open -R <folder>` (the folder selected in its parent's window) rather than opened, so no package is ever launched; the list read from the live config on each request; the alias flag in the Finder info refused as well; (b) keep `open <file>` and add refusals: any OpenWith attribute, the Finder-info alias flag, macOS's own package test, a symlink to a folder, the live list. Recommended (a): it removes the Launch Services choice instead of chasing its inputs, which three reviews in a row found new ways around; the costs are that each type names its program once in `behavior.yml`, and the project card's folder control shows the folder selected in Finder instead of opening its window. - Q2 landed 2026-09-11 from worktree `q2` (wip f9aa899, cherry-pick onto main, clean; one orchestrator fix of a defect the new layer found in the application: `views/focus/QuickAdd.svelte` wrote a follow-up as `{ followup }` while `config/manifest-schema.yml` names `followup.do` and `followup.after`, so `writes/manifest.ts` refused the field and the page said "saved" over an untouched file; the same refusal hit the ticker's `done` on a project follow-up, which clears with `{ followup: '' }`. The fix: quick add writes `followup.do` (the editor's `SHORTHAND` expands a bare note into the map); `writes/manifest.ts` accepts a schema group's parent name, `followup`, for clearing only, since the file may hold the group as a note, a map or a list and the editor can clear a whole key of any shape, and refuses a value for it with its own reason; `QuickAdd.svelte` and `CommandCenter.svelte` report a write that was refused whole as not saved, reading `answer.refused`, rather than "saved" with an empty list; four cases in `tests/server/writes.test.ts`); the commit follows this rewrite. Before the fix a manifest naming a lane that does not exist passed with zero findings and its card was drawn on no lane, which is how four demo manifests were silently off the board; (2) the browser layer serves whatever `build/` holds, and nothing checks the build is current; (3) `tests/browser/.hub` is written into the checkout (gitignored) and a crashed run leaves it stale; (4) the temporary hub copy is never removed (136 KB per run); (5) five CSS classes of `Lanes.svelte`, `ProjectCard.svelte` and `EntryCard.svelte` are load-bearing for the specs (`.lane`, `.lane-name`, `.slot`, `.grip`, `.line`); (6) the specs depend on the demo holding a past deadline, two lanes with cards and three tasks, and nothing asserts those preconditions; (7) a quick-add follow-up on a project that already carries a note replaces the note rather than adding a second one, and `done` on any follow-up line of a project clears every note of that project, since the ticker target carries no note index; (8) `playwright.config.ts` is outside the lint's project service and is in its ignore list; (9) `tests/browser/words.ts` repeats `t()`'s interpolation because `state/text.ts` pulls a rune module Node cannot load. - Axel's question of 2026-09-11, whether an Opus design agent writing briefs for a Sonnet implementer would cut tokens: answered no. The two regime rows show tokens tracking tool calls (165 calls 277k, 57 calls 174k), so a designer agent is a third run on top of the brief, which already is the concrete design; the saving can only come from Sonnet's price per token. The O16 Sonnet trial runs with the brief as it stands; if it passes, the model is chosen per package by kind (Sonnet for a server-side, fully specified package; Opus where the shell, the layout tree or open design calls are touched), and after two Sonnet passes the rule goes into the `plan-orchestration` skill. Its own first line: NOT DONE, `npm test` and the 8791 check could not run in its sandbox (`listen EPERM` on 127.0.0.1, `EMFILE` on the watchers, and a write to the temp dir refused by its patch tool), and three acceptance items were incomplete (the three-segment capacity meter, the log path ladder, the pill and rail badge tests). Outside the sandbox the worktree passed every unit gate (86 files 1401 tests, check 0/0, lint, format, ASCII). The diff read found, beyond those: no head comment on any of the fifteen new files; the pill's words built in `state/hpc.svelte.ts` as a literal English string rather than through `t()` (the catalog holds `js.slurm.pill_running`); raw `<button>` and `<table>` markup instead of the primitives; the host `utwente` hardcoded in four places; `src/server.ts` re-reading `behavior.yml` by hand through a dynamic import instead of `loadConfig`; `durationSeconds` duplicated between `server/hpc/parse.ts` and `state/hpc.ts`; the `hpc` catalog group moved from `text.yml` to `text-oculus.yml` with the old keys kept beside new duplicates of them; Svelte markup compacted onto single lines; thin tests (two cases per file). That is more than eight fixes at landing against the Opus rows' zero to five, so the ruling applies: O26 is redone on Opus from the same brief in a fresh `o26` worktree at 55309b1, both costs are recorded, and the trial stops unless Axel says otherwise. What the trial also showed about the harness itself: Codex's workspace-write sandbox cannot bind a local port, which the oculus suite needs (the socket, watcher and pty tests), so a Codex agent can never run `npm test` here without `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access = true` or a policy that allows `listen`; that is a harness fact, separate from the model's output.
